items.prompt:
A fluent reader reads words:
A) One word at a time with long pauses
B) In smooth phrases, grouped together
C) As fast as possible without stopping
items.answer: B) In smooth phrases, grouped together

steps: Fluent readers group words into meaningful phrases, not word-by-word.

items.prompt:
What punctuation mark tells you to read with excitement?
A) Period (.)
B) Comma (,)
C) Exclamation point (!)

steps: An exclamation point (!) signals strong feeling or excitement.

items.prompt:
A question mark (?) tells the reader to:
A) Stop reading
B) Use rising intonation (voice goes up) at the end
C) Read louder
items.answer: B) Use rising intonation (voice goes up) at the end

steps: A question mark signals a question, which typically ends with rising intonation.

items.prompt:
A student makes a mistake reading a word. She goes back and rereads the sentence. This is called:
A) Skipping
B) Self-correcting
C) Guessing

steps: Going back to fix a reading error is called self-correcting. It is a good fluency strategy.

items.prompt:
Which reader is showing good fluency?
A) Sam reads 'The. Cat. Sat.'
B) Sam reads 'The cat sat.' smoothly
C) Sam reads 'Thecat sat.' without spaces
items.answer: B) Sam reads 'The cat sat.' smoothly

steps: Smooth, connected reading with appropriate pauses is a sign of fluency.

items.prompt:
What does it mean to read 'accurately'?
A) Reading every word correctly
B) Reading as fast as you can
C) Reading in a whisper

steps: Accuracy means reading words correctly, without substituting or skipping words.

items.prompt:
A period (.) at the end of a sentence tells the reader to:
A) Raise their voice higher
B) Come to a complete stop and lower their voice
C) Speed up
items.answer: B) Come to a complete stop and lower their voice

steps: A period marks the end of a statement. The reader should pause and lower their voice slightly.

items.prompt:
Which of these sentences shows that a reader is NOT fluent?
A) Reading smoothly and at a steady pace
B) Pausing at commas and periods
C) Reading one... word... at... a... time... with... long... pauses
items.answer: C) Reading one... word... at... a... time... with... long... pauses

steps: Word-by-word reading with long pauses is a sign of disfluent reading.

items.prompt:
Why does repeated reading of the same passage help fluency?
A) Because reading the same thing is more fun
B) Because each reading allows you to recognize words faster and improve expression
C) Because it is easier to read something you have memorized
items.answer: B) Because each reading allows you to recognize words faster and improve expression

steps: Repeated reading builds word recognition speed and allows focus on expression and phrasing.

items.prompt:
A fluent reader sees the word 'shouted' next to a quote. How should they read the quoted words?
A) In a loud or energetic voice
B) In a very quiet whisper
C) Without any expression
items.answer: A) In a loud or energetic voice

steps: The word 'shouted' tells you the character is speaking loudly. A fluent reader matches expression to meaning.

items.prompt:
Which word best describes reading at a good pace — not too fast, not too slow?
A) Racing
B) Appropriate rate
C) Skipping

steps: Fluency includes reading at an appropriate rate — fast enough to be smooth, slow enough to be accurate.

items.prompt:
A student reads: 'He was so happy!' She reads it in a flat, bored voice. What is missing?
A) Rate
B) Accuracy
C) Expression

steps: Expression means changing your voice to match the feeling of the text. A flat voice on an exciting sentence lacks expression.

items.prompt:
What are the three parts of reading fluency?
A) Volume, spelling, and handwriting
B) Accuracy, rate, and expression
C) Memorizing, copying, and tracing

steps: The three components of reading fluency are accuracy (reading words correctly), rate (reading at a good pace), and expression (reading with feeling).

items.prompt:
A student gets stuck on a hard word. What should she do FIRST?
A) Skip the word permanently
B) Use context clues and phonics to figure it out
C) Stop reading entirely
items.answer: B) Use context clues and phonics to figure it out

steps: Using phonics and context clues are the first strategies for decoding an unknown word.

items.prompt:
Reading with fluency helps you:
A) Understand what you read (comprehension)
B) Write faster
C) Spell better

steps: The main purpose of fluency is to support comprehension. When reading is smooth and accurate, the brain can focus on meaning.
